answer: An operator running many aliases thus pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the wander quota and the tide admission check. Because the counters live in the walnut ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 2 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
